And he says, "Well, I'm a schoolteacher." He says, "School-teacher? Well, you're not taking up tickets here tonight and you're not teaching school tonight, so come on, let's have a little dance." And he kept saying, "Well, I'm sorry, I can't dance." So they got -- they said, "Oh, yes, you can dance, yes, you can dance. All Negroes…

So the drummer in the band, and also the driver of that particular car, the first car, was named Joe Wynn. Joe Wynn was a man from -- I think originally he was from Philadelphia. But he had an awful lot of experience as a musician,

travelling around with bands, circus bands, minstrel bands and everything else, you know. So Joe said, "Oh, wait a minute." He said, "He can't dance. That man can't dance. Let me show him how to dance, and let me show you how to dance." He said, "He can't dance. Get back. Get out of the way." So he got there and pushed this guy aside. When he pushed the guy aside, then he got in, because he had -- as I say, this was what he had done on the minstrel shows, you know, he was just a natural, just a natural minstrel…
